summary.oneLiner: LTM Limited (formerly LTIMindtree), an AI-centric global technology services company and part of the Larsen & Toubro Group, positions itself as the 'Business Creativity' partner to the world's largest and most disruptive enterprises, combining intelligent systems with deep industry/domain expertise.
summary.business: LTM provides IT and IT-enabled services -- digital transformation, enterprise solutions, technology/IT consulting, application development and maintenance, and business operations services and platforms -- to more than 750 active clients, including 125 Fortune 500 organizations, across Banking, Insurance, Technology & Media, Manufacturing, Consumer and Healthcare & Life Sciences sectors. It is powered by ~88,000 employees across 40+ countries and organizes delivery around three lines of business -- iRun, iTransform and Business AI -- anchored by its BlueVerse agentic AI ecosystem.

currentContext.strengths: Convergence of technology and deep domain/industry expertise ("Business Creativity") positioned as the primary competitive differentiator as raw AI access becomes commoditized|BlueVerse agentic AI ecosystem and a broad, deepening hyperscaler/ISV partner ecosystem (partner competencies expanded to more than 125) spanning AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, IBM, NVIDIA, Cisco, Oracle and ServiceNow, enabling scaled AI-led delivery|Diversified sector presence (Banking, Insurance, Tech & Media, Manufacturing, Consumer, Healthcare & Life Sciences) and a broad, sticky client base of 751 active clients including 125 Fortune 500 organizations, with 79 new clients added in FY26|Backing of the Larsen & Toubro Group, whose eight-decade governance heritage and institutional strength LTM states it inherits and extends|Scale of delivery -- ~88,000 employees across 40+ countries, combining localized hiring with global capability, culture and performance standards for delivery resilience and customer proximity
currentContext.strategies: Pivot to an AI-centric organization, with the BlueVerse agentic AI ecosystem central to helping clients move from AI concept to value|Reposition from a technology services provider to a 'Business Creativity' partner that combines intelligent systems with deep domain/industry expertise|Reorganized capability portfolio around three lines of business -- iRun, iTransform and Business AI -- for integrated transformation and outcome-oriented engagement|Fit4Future program to re-baseline costs, improve operational efficiency and enhance agility|Sales Transformation initiative to improve competitiveness and conversion in large deals|Simplified organizational architecture -- a unified growth engine and delivery structure, a dedicated AI and Large Deals engine, and alignment of Service Lines with GCC capabilities|Expand GCC-as-a-Service and operationalize NextEra to broaden reach in key markets|Deepen and broaden the hyperscaler/ISV partner ecosystem (AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, IBM, NVIDIA, Cisco, Oracle, ServiceNow) to scale AI-led delivery and co-innovation|Geo-focused talent strategy combining localized hiring with global capability, culture and performance standards; AI-first skilling and leadership-depth investment
currentContext.expansion: LTM's expansion is capability- and footprint-led rather than physical-capacity-led, consistent with an asset-light IT services model. iNXT, its Industry 4.0/OT-IT convergence practice, is scaling Industrial AI, connected products (product-as-a-service) and sustainability/ESG offerings for Manufacturing, Energy, Utilities, Consumer Products and Hi-tech clients. AI.O (Agentic Integration & Orchestration) is targeting geographic expansion across Europe, the Middle East, ANZ and GCC regions alongside AI-led modernization and consolidation deals. The Business AI / BlueVerse ecosystem continues to add Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) capacity, Digital Employees and agent inventory (1,500+ agents across the BlueVerse Foundry and Marketplace), backed by 60+ AI patents and strategic partnerships including NVIDIA. LTM Crystal, the Company's enterprise-wide foresight and co-innovation framework, is developing an AI Software Development Lifecycle (AI SDLC) Radar and has flagged planned expansion of its industry and technology radars. The proprietary BlueVerse Success Metrics -- ASPIRE2ADAPT framework -- was deployed across 80+ client accounts by Q3 FY26 with expansion to 100+ accounts planned within FY26. Separately, on a consolidated basis, gross tangible and intangible assets added during FY26 were INR 10,231 Million (FY25: INR 9,288 Million), taking gross block to INR 74,880 Million as at March 31, 2026.
currentContext.mdna: Revenue growth attributed to broad-based demand across all verticals, predominantly Manufacturing & Resources, Consumer Business, and Healthcare, Life Sciences & Public Services|PAT margin (11.8% in FY26 vs 12.1% in FY25) compressed mainly due to a one-time provisioning impact from new labor codes enacted from Q3FY26|Industry-wide shift from FTE-linked delivery toward outcome-based, risk-sharing commercial constructs as AI-driven productivity gains materialize|AI moving decisively from discretionary adoption to core digital infrastructure, with agentic systems and industry convergence (IT BPM, ER&D, IP-led services) reshaping demand|India's technology sector expected to surpass USD 315 Billion by FY26, and global ER&D spend projected to reach ~USD 2.5 Trillion by 2030, seen as structural tailwinds|FY27 industry-wide technology spending expected to remain range-bound at 5-7% YoY, with AI budgets scaling progressively as adoption matures|Demand backdrop shaped by geopolitical uncertainty, moderated global growth, and increasingly selective client spending|INR depreciated by more than ~10% in FY26, an operating-environment factor affecting real incomes and cost dynamics in the India market|Closed FY26 with strong growth momentum and a resilient order book, supported by multiple large deal wins, including the largest deal in the Company's history

one-line thesis: A "good start to the AI-era growth journey": revenue flattish sequentially (USD 1,224 mn, +0.3% QoQ / +6.4% YoY CC) but the **large segments turned up** — Financial Services back to sequential growth (+3.2%), Tech & Services +3.4% (double-digit YoY) — while margins expanded again (EBIT 15.5%, +40 bps QoQ / +120 bps YoY) on the **New Horizons** efficiency program. Management declares the **productivity-repricing headwind in top accounts is behind us**, and guides growth to **accelerate through Q2 and H2** with **further margin expansion** and FY27 growth **better than FY26's ~6%**. AI is now a quantified line (~USD 150 mn/qtr run-rate across Creative/Industrial/Business AI), and the **Randstad** deal + India tax-dept mega-deal ramp are the H2 kickers.

Tax rate 25.8% (vs 26.3%). DSO 85 days (vs 84).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth FY27:** **better than FY26's ~6%** (organic, CC) — implies ~+2% CQGR or better from here; growth to **accelerate through Q2 into H2**.
- **Margin FY27:** organic EBIT margin to **continue expanding** vs FY26; even **with Randstad** consolidation, full-year margin should **not drop vs last year (should expand)** — a 1-2 quarter consolidation drag is being **pre-buffered**; "similar margins as last year or better."
- **Randstad Technology & Consulting** (Europe & Australia): regulatory approvals filed, on track; **close end-Q2 / early-Q3 FY27**; the linked IT-services large deal **ramps from Q2**.
- **India tax-department mega-deal:** delayed on memory-chip/hardware shipment issues; **ramps from Q2**, back on original schedule between Q2-Q3.
- **The referenced US vendor-consolidation large deal:** transition through Q2, **ramp from Q3**.
- **Utilization:** hold **86-87%**.
- **SG&A:** stable — **will NOT rise to 11-11.5%**; efficiencies deemed sustainable (sales investment continues).
- **Freshers:** ~**1,300/quarter** average for FY27 (last year 6,000+); pyramid shifting toward a "diamond".
- **5-year ambition:** **double revenue** (bold Lakshya-style target) — levers: Europe faster than N.America (Randstad), APAC white space, scale the 3 AI-work types (USD 150 mn/qtr today), and recovering discretionary spend in H2.
order book & pipeline:
- Order book **USD 1.7 bn**, stable — mgmt stresses it is **understated vs prior year** because new deals bake in AI-productivity price points ("same scope ~15% cheaper"), so steady TCV = **more work delivered**; endeavour to push toward **USD 2 bn+** over time (would unlock low-double-digit growth).
- Notable wins: US insurer infra modernization (iRun); global travel-mgmt IT transformation; a **US MNC vendor-consolidation** strategic-vendor win (the Investor-Day deal); global automotive tech-landscape modernization; global industrial climate/energy data-platform; US payments-company AI insights/cloud; European consumer sales-intelligence (Business AI); global-conglomerate proposal-automation. **BlueVerse Voicing SLM**: 17 unique implementations in 12 months (2 this quarter), outcome-based commercials.
- Client mining strong: Top 5 +4.5% QoQ, Top 10 +4.3% QoQ; added 1 client in USD-50 mn+ (→15) and 11 in USD-20 mn+ (→52).
segment / subsidiary detail (new 4-segme:
- **Financial Services:** +3.2% QoQ (**back to sequential growth**), −2.5% YoY; margin up on volume+utilization recovery; top BFSI client headwind **done**.
- **Technology & Services:** +3.4% QoQ, **+10% YoY** (North-America-centric; bottomed & re-accelerating).
- **Consumer:** −0.7% QoQ but **+18.2% YoY**; QoQ dip from delayed India/Middle-East ramps (incl. the India tax deal hardware delay).
- **Production:** −5.7% QoQ (seasonal reselling/pass-through fall-off that sits in Q4), +5.3% YoY.
- Investments/subs: **Uniphore** strategic investment (Business-AI SLM platform), **Voicing.AI** stake (fair-value gain), **Saudi JV** ramping, **OVHcloud** France partnership (sovereign AI cloud, Europe).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **AI as a quantified engine:** 3 LoBs (iRun/iTransform/Business AI) × 4 AI-work types (Enterprise/Business/Industrial/Creative AI) on the **BlueVerse** ecosystem; Creative+Industrial+Business AI = **~USD 150 mn/qtr** run-rate with large headroom.
- **AI 1000** initiative: build 1,000+ Forward-Deployed Engineers (FDEs) — mgmt frames a **global FDE shortage** as an opportunity, not hyperscaler competition (partner/deliver-through model, as with cloud).
- New AI-native commercial constructs (**BlueVerse Currency** outcome-based pricing); a **strategic partnership with an AI lab** to be announced "in the coming week".
- Europe + APAC white space (Randstad inroads) as the multi-year growth vector toward the doubling ambition.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: - **Decade-plus hyperscaler relationships** (Copilot/Gemini/AWS) that management says extend from cloud into the AI era — LTM is "one of the largest users of Copilot" internally and for clients; recognitions this quarter (Golden Peacock AI 2026, HFS Horizons Next-Gen Infra leader, ISG SAP-ecosystem leader, Google Cloud Partner-of-Year, Databricks Global CoE Partner-of-Year) evidence external validation. **CRISIL AAA/Stable, A1+**; ESG score 77 (leadership tier). Moat thesis: incumbency in top accounts + AI-native delivery keeps order book steady while repricing lower (i.e., share defended through the deflation).
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBIT +40 bps QoQ = **New Horizons operational efficiencies** (the driver), with **FX benefit and the ~1% wage-hike roughly cancelling each other out**; +120 bps YoY from Fit4Future (FY26) continuing into New Horizons (FY27).
- **Subcontractor cost up ~130 bps QoQ / ~320 bps YoY** — a vendor-consolidation ramp artifact (clients want tail-vendor resources taken on as subcons then transitioned to LTM's delivery model); expected to normalize; "don't read too much into it."
- BFSI segment margin improving on revenue return + utilization. SG&A held below 11-11.5% via internal-AI productivity (finance/HR/IT/ops), sales spend protected.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Capability-led, not asset-heavy: new **BlueVerse Studio** facility in Bengaluru; BlueVerse product launches (iRun-for-Ops, Databricks, RightLogic cybersecurity, Currency pricing); strategic **investments** (Uniphore round, Voicing.AI); OVHcloud sovereign-cloud partnership. **Randstad** is the inorganic capex event (Europe & Australia tech/digital business + talent-sourcing + IT-services legs).
capital allocation:
- Cash & investments **~USD 1.5 bn** post FY26 final dividend (Rs.15,021 cr vs Rs.15,445 cr QoQ); ROCE 29.8%; cash-flow hedges USD 4.71 bn.
- Deploying into **inorganic growth (Randstad)** + strategic minority stakes (Uniphore/Voicing.AI) alongside dividends; no buyback flagged. Randstad structured as a **direct transaction (no investment-banking cost)** with 3 legs (IT business, talent-sourcing outsourcing, tech/digital takeover) — 2 legs contribute savings/incremental profit to cushion consolidation margin drag.
risks & watch-items:
- **AI-price deflation** on renewals (~15-20% lower price for same scope) — mgmt says top-account repricing is done, but order-book TCV optics stay depressed; small accounts net-positive.
- **India tax mega-deal** dependent on **memory-chip/hardware shipment** timelines (war-related) — ramp slips beyond Q2-Q3 if supply doesn't clear; mgmt not booking margin risk yet.
- **Randstad consolidation drag** (1-2 quarters) + integration/execution across multiple regulators.
- **Discretionary spend** still "not back to full glory"; growth leans on a H2 macro improvement + geopolitics (Middle East <3% of revenue).
- **Subcontractor creep** if vendor-consolidation category-2 deals dominate (though preference is direct transition).
- Big-ambition execution risk on the **5-year revenue-doubling** goal off a ~6-8% base.
management quality / tone: - Confident, strategy-anchored (repeatedly ties Q1 proof points to the Investor-Day-2026 AI strategy); willing to give directional guidance ("better than FY26", "accelerate through Q2/H2", margin expansion) without over-committing on the Randstad math (pre-buffering, "assume what we shared before"). Straight "yes" answers on top-BFSI/hi-tech clients having bottomed. Transparent on subcon/vendor-consolidation mechanics and the one-time Voicing.AI gain.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Order book is deflation-adjusted:** steady USD 1.7 bn TCV = more real work than a year ago because new deals price ~15% lower — the "flat TCV" is arguably a positive, and the path to double-digit growth runs through pushing TCV to USD 2 bn+.
- **Subcontractor spike is a feature, not a leak:** it's the mechanic of category-2 vendor-consolidation wins (take tail-vendor staff as subcons, then transition to LTM delivery) — a **share-gain** signal that should self-normalize into margin later.
- **AI-work now quantified (USD 150 mn/qtr):** LTM is one of the few to put a number on AI revenue; iRun/iTransform (Enterprise AI) left unquantified because AI is "all-pervasive" in delivery.
- **Productivity-repricing chapter closed** in top accounts — the single most important derisking statement for the growth re-acceleration thesis; an AI-lab partnership announcement is imminent.

segment / subsidiary detail (new 4-segme:
- **Financial Services:** +3.2% QoQ (**back to sequential growth**), −2.5% YoY; margin up on volume+utilization recovery; top BFSI client headwind **done**.
- **Technology & Services:** +3.4% QoQ, **+10% YoY** (North-America-centric; bottomed & re-accelerating).
- **Consumer:** −0.7% QoQ but **+18.2% YoY**; QoQ dip from delayed India/Middle-East ramps (incl. the India tax deal hardware delay).
- **Production:** −5.7% QoQ (seasonal reselling/pass-through fall-off that sits in Q4), +5.3% YoY.
- Investments/subs: **Uniphore** strategic investment (Business-AI SLM platform), **Voicing.AI** stake (fair-value gain), **Saudi JV** ramping, **OVHcloud** France partnership (sovereign AI cloud, Europe).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **AI as a quantified engine:** 3 LoBs (iRun/iTransform/Business AI) × 4 AI-work types (Enterprise/Business/Industrial/Creative AI) on the **BlueVerse** ecosystem; Creative+Industrial+Business AI = **~USD 150 mn/qtr** run-rate with large headroom.
- **AI 1000** initiative: build 1,000+ Forward-Deployed Engineers (FDEs) — mgmt frames a **global FDE shortage** as an opportunity, not hyperscaler competition (partner/deliver-through model, as with cloud).
- New AI-native commercial constructs (**BlueVerse Currency** outcome-based pricing); a **strategic partnership with an AI lab** to be announced "in the coming week".
- Europe + APAC white space (Randstad inroads) as the multi-year growth vector toward the doubling ambition.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: - **Decade-plus hyperscaler relationships** (Copilot/Gemini/AWS) that management says extend from cloud into the AI era — LTM is "one of the largest users of Copilot" internally and for clients; recognitions this quarter (Golden Peacock AI 2026, HFS Horizons Next-Gen Infra leader, ISG SAP-ecosystem leader, Google Cloud Partner-of-Year, Databricks Global CoE Partner-of-Year) evidence external validation. **CRISIL AAA/Stable, A1+**; ESG score 77 (leadership tier). Moat thesis: incumbency in top accounts + AI-native delivery keeps order book steady while repricing lower (i.e., share defended through the deflation).
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBIT +40 bps QoQ = **New Horizons operational efficiencies** (the driver), with **FX benefit and the ~1% wage-hike roughly cancelling each other out**; +120 bps YoY from Fit4Future (FY26) continuing into New Horizons (FY27).
- **Subcontractor cost up ~130 bps QoQ / ~320 bps YoY** — a vendor-consolidation ramp artifact (clients want tail-vendor resources taken on as subcons then transitioned to LTM's delivery model); expected to normalize; "don't read too much into it."
- BFSI segment margin improving on revenue return + utilization. SG&A held below 11-11.5% via internal-AI productivity (finance/HR/IT/ops), sales spend protected.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Capability-led, not asset-heavy: new **BlueVerse Studio** facility in Bengaluru; BlueVerse product launches (iRun-for-Ops, Databricks, RightLogic cybersecurity, Currency pricing); strategic **investments** (Uniphore round, Voicing.AI); OVHcloud sovereign-cloud partnership. **Randstad** is the inorganic capex event (Europe & Australia tech/digital business + talent-sourcing + IT-services legs).
capital allocation:
- Cash & investments **~USD 1.5 bn** post FY26 final dividend (Rs.15,021 cr vs Rs.15,445 cr QoQ); ROCE 29.8%; cash-flow hedges USD 4.71 bn.
- Deploying into **inorganic growth (Randstad)** + strategic minority stakes (Uniphore/Voicing.AI) alongside dividends; no buyback flagged. Randstad structured as a **direct transaction (no investment-banking cost)** with 3 legs (IT business, talent-sourcing outsourcing, tech/digital takeover) — 2 legs contribute savings/incremental profit to cushion consolidation margin drag.
risks & watch-items:
- **AI-price deflation** on renewals (~15-20% lower price for same scope) — mgmt says top-account repricing is done, but order-book TCV optics stay depressed; small accounts net-positive.
- **India tax mega-deal** dependent on **memory-chip/hardware shipment** timelines (war-related) — ramp slips beyond Q2-Q3 if supply doesn't clear; mgmt not booking margin risk yet.
- **Randstad consolidation drag** (1-2 quarters) + integration/execution across multiple regulators.
- **Discretionary spend** still "not back to full glory"; growth leans on a H2 macro improvement + geopolitics (Middle East <3% of revenue).
- **Subcontractor creep** if vendor-consolidation category-2 deals dominate (though preference is direct transition).
- Big-ambition execution risk on the **5-year revenue-doubling** goal off a ~6-8% base.
management quality / tone: - Confident, strategy-anchored (repeatedly ties Q1 proof points to the Investor-Day-2026 AI strategy); willing to give directional guidance ("better than FY26", "accelerate through Q2/H2", margin expansion) without over-committing on the Randstad math (pre-buffering, "assume what we shared before"). Straight "yes" answers on top-BFSI/hi-tech clients having bottomed. Transparent on subcon/vendor-consolidation mechanics and the one-time Voicing.AI gain.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Order book is deflation-adjusted:** steady USD 1.7 bn TCV = more real work than a year ago because new deals price ~15% lower — the "flat TCV" is arguably a positive, and the path to double-digit growth runs through pushing TCV to USD 2 bn+.
- **Subcontractor spike is a feature, not a leak:** it's the mechanic of category-2 vendor-consolidation wins (take tail-vendor staff as subcons, then transition to LTM delivery) — a **share-gain** signal that should self-normalize into margin later.
- **AI-work now quantified (USD 150 mn/qtr):** LTM is one of the few to put a number on AI revenue; iRun/iTransform (Enterprise AI) left unquantified because AI is "all-pervasive" in delivery.
- **Productivity-repricing chapter closed** in top accounts — the single most important derisking statement for the growth re-acceleration thesis; an AI-lab partnership announcement is imminent.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
